clue.text: Fancy hot bedrooms are not groovy

definitions.note: a gun barrel with no spiral grooves cut into it

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or contrived, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An estate agent's verdict: the fancy, overheated bedrooms are a bit dull and unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' reads as sixties slang for cool, but here it is literal: grooves, as in the rifling inside a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bored gun has a barrel without rifling, so its bore has no grooves at all.

clue.text: Wife not interested tonight? I can't manage

definitions.meaning: the surface picture: a spouse who would rather just go to sleep in bed
the business sense: a partner who puts money in but takes no part in running the firm

explanation.walkthrough: The bedroom scene is the red herring; the phrase is a business term for an investor with no management role.
explanation.definitionFit: In business a sleeping partner invests capital but is not involved in running the company, so cannot manage it.

clue.text: Stench of Iberian river, bubble rising to the surface

indicators.note: in a down entry the bubble floats up from the bottom of the river's name to the top

parts.note: a bubble is round, the shape of the letter O
the Douro flows through Spain and Portugal to the Atlantic at Porto

explanation.surface: A river in Spain or Portugal smells foul, with gas bubbling up from its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The O shaped like a bubble moves from the bottom of the river's name to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, and in everyday use it usually means an unpleasant one, a stench.

clue.text: Ornamental tracery work probed by judge

indicators.note: the judge's letters go into the work's letters, as a probe goes into something

parts.note: to toil is to work hard
a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: An architect's report: decorative stonework examined closely by an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gothic architecture a trefoil is a three-lobed decorative opening in window tracery.

clue.text: Out of helmet take a large pastry

indicators.note: with 'take' this says some letters are removed from the helmet
with 'Out of' this says the following letters are taken away from the helmet

parts.note: a balaclava is a knitted head covering, a helmet in the older sense
A as written, then L for large

explanation.surface: An instruction: from your headgear, pull out a big cake.
explanation.walkthrough: BACLAVA is an accepted spelling of baklava, the Middle Eastern pastry; the balaclava is a woollen hood covering head and neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Baclava is a sweet dessert of layered filo dough with nuts and honey syrup.

clue.text: A man draws this stack of hay and wood

parts.note: a rick is a haystack
shaw is an old word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a rural scene: a haystack and some trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' suggests sketching, but the man is pulling the vehicle along.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger cart pulled by a man on foot.

clue.text: Teacher preparing me a talk — me! Yuk, it's unbelievable

definitions.note: the phrase is a whole exclamation of disbelief

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: preparing a talk means putting it together, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
both are cries of disgust

explanation.surface: A lecturer grumbles about having to write a talk for himself: disgusting, unbelievable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scornful retort meaning the speaker finds what was said ridiculous or incredible.

clue.text: There's malaria spreading: call for help

indicators.note: a disease spreading moves about, and so do these letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outbreak of malaria prompts an urgent appeal for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the alarm is to warn others of danger and summon assistance.

clue.text: Support each other to win hearts, blocking pig killer

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the answer

indicators.note: the words before sit in the middle of the pig killer, blocking it

parts.note: pig-sticking is hunting boar with a spear, so a sticker kills pigs
taken as written
to get something is to win it

explanation.surface: Teammates resolve to back one another, winning hearts by stopping a pig butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to stay loyal and help one another through difficulties.

clue.text: Flower sends submariner into an ecstasy

indicators.note: the submariner's name goes inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A blossom sends a sailor from a submarine into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a garden plant of the buttercup family grown for its bright blooms.

clue.text: One shied, caught out concealing scam

definitions.note: the noun phrase means a thing thrown at

indicators.note: the scam is hidden within the word out

parts.note: taken as written
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: Someone flinched, was caught out and covered up a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shied' looks like timid, but means thrown: at a coconut shy, a British fairground stall, you throw balls to knock coconuts off stands. C is the cricket abbreviation for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: At a fairground shy the targets pelted with balls are coconuts, so a coconut is a thing thrown at.

clue.text: Cosmetics salesperson from America comes back to make a big bang

definitions.note: an exploding star, a noun phrase like the answer

indicators.note: the whole string is read backwards, returning to its start

parts.note: an Avon rep sells the Avon brand of cosmetics door to door
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: A door-to-door beauty seller returns from the States to make a splash.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is the colossal explosion of a dying star, briefly outshining its galaxy.

clue.text: Tree's total area collecting carbon

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A surveyor measures a tree's overall area and how much carbon it absorbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree of the genus Rhus, whose berries make a tangy spice.

clue.text: Accent presumably from the south-west

parts.note: an accent coming from somewhere is presumably heading to the opposite point
the point opposite the south-west on the compass is the north-east, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A West Country burr, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The south-west suggests a regional voice from Devon or Cornwall, but it is a compass bearing: travelling from there takes you to the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent and tone both mean the particular quality or stress of a voice.

clue.text: Armada, circling a minute lifeboat, stalls

definitions.note: a plural noun; the answer is a market made of many stalls

indicators.note: the fleet surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
taken as written
Noah's ark saved its passengers from the Flood

explanation.surface: A war fleet surrounds a tiny lifeboat, which stops dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalls' reads as a verb about the lifeboat's engine, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open-air gathering of stalls selling second-hand goods.

clue.text: All the officers here succeeded in moving my trial

definitions.note: the answer is the register where every officer appears

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded goes inside the rearranged letters
these words are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer reports that a court case was a success in shifting his trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Army List is the official published register of all commissioned officers in the British Army.

clue.text: One takes people through specialist trial

indicators.note: the pieces run through the middle of the specialist

parts.note: an expert is a specialist
I is the Roman numeral one
men are people

explanation.surface: A specialist guides a group through a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a test carried out to try something out, so it is a trial.

clue.text: Ring performer has millions on top of a little gold

explanation.surface: A boxer has a fortune as well as a bit of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests boxing or circus, but this ring is the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull in the arena.

clue.text: Favoured remedy in no way peculiar

parts.note: taken as written
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A pet cure that is not strange at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet scheme or a quack medicine someone swears by, a cure of their own.

clue.text: Writing about sporting blunder in bad visibility

indicators.note: the writing is turned about, back to front

parts.note: MS is a manuscript
OG is an own goal in football

explanation.surface: A report about a fumble in the match blamed on poor light.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is thick polluted fog that cuts how far one can see.

clue.text: Fat boy meets another finally across river

indicators.note: the boy's letters are laid across the river, enclosing it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
another boy, and its final letter

explanation.surface: A plump lad meets a friend on the far side of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another boy, so its final letter is that word's last.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy is a colloquial adjective for plump or overweight, from lard, pig fat.

clue.text: Pole is three times wounded — he takes high risks

definitions.note: a person, as the answer is

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'High' is literal: this risk-taker flies new aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies untried aircraft to assess them, a dangerous job high in the sky.

clue.text: Lacy border seemingly good on bed

parts.note: pi is short for pious, which is goodness for show
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A frilly edge that looks nice on a bed.

clue.text: We hear Oscar's agent did lose all control

indicators.note: the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: the agent would run, or manage, Oscar Wilde

explanation.definitionFit: To run wild is to behave without restraint or discipline.

clue.text: One who's withdrawn from class in recycling

indicators.note: the class abbreviation sits inside the recycling word

parts.note: reuse is a form of recycling
CL is a standard abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A pupil pulled out of lessons during a recycling project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn from class' reads as one phrase, but 'from' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives apart from society, withdrawn and solitary.

clue.text: End striker's loan period for second leg

definitions.meaning: a football club's forward on loan elsewhere comes back when the loan ends, and his comeback is a game
a tie played home and away, the second of the two games

explanation.walkthrough: The football transfer story is a play on the phrase: the striker's return ends his loan, and the fixture itself is a return.
explanation.definitionFit: A return match is the second game between the same teams, as in the second leg of a cup tie.
